newsitem.title: MEXICO: Counterfeit bills a growing problem in Guadalajara.
newsitem.headline: Counterfeit bills a growing problem in Guadalajara.

text.p: Merchants in the western city of Guadalajara are so fed up with a growing problem of counterfeit money that they have asked the central bank for help, a local business leader said Thursday.

"We have asked Banco de Mexico to come up with some kind of solution to the situation and for training to identify false bills because it has become a very serious daily problem," Horacio Gonzalez Pardo, president of the local Chamber of Commerce, told Reuters. He said the problem became particularly acute in 1996 in Guadalajara, the second-largest city in Mexico and the third-largest industrial center.
Small and medium-sized commerical establishments have been hardest hit, mostly restaurants, clothing stores and auto repair services, Gonzalez said.
"We identified about four or five cases this past month with large amounts of false money," said Martin Reyes, a manager at the Million Dollar currency exchange house.
"We're talking about 200,000 pesos in one month at just one business."
Reyes said the quality of counterfeit bills has increased notably in the past year.
